subject.title: [Bug]: Usage history assigns events to wrong local day across DST transitions

question: Should maintainers proceed with the open additive IANA `timeZone` usage RPC fix in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103097, or choose a different compatibility shape?
rationale: The bug is source-backed, but the live issue carries the protected `maintainer` label and the fix changes a public Gateway/UI request contract.

options.title: Review and land current fix candidate
options.body: Proceed with the open PR if its additive `timeZone` contract, fallback behavior, tests, and proof satisfy maintainer expectations.

options.title: Revise the protocol shape first
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for changes if maintainers want a different field name, fallback rule, generated-client behavior, or test boundary.

options.title: Defer as accepted limitation
options.body: Keep or close this only by explicit maintainer decision if fixed-offset local history is acceptable for now despite known DST analytics drift.

recommendation.title: Review and land current fix candidate
recommendation.body: Proceed with the open PR if its additive `timeZone` contract, fallback behavior, tests, and proof satisfy maintainer expectations.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned to the issue, authored the Profile surface that documented the limitation, and opened the current fix candidate.
